diagnostics.notes: Both extractions match their sources: A reports a negative adiponectin-HbA1C correlation (sentence 14) in perimenopausal women; B reports a positive correlation (r = 0.19, P = 0.032, sentence 9) in type-2 DM patients. Same exposure (adiponectin), same outcome (HbA1c), same contrast type (association), so the pair is comparable. The directions are genuinely opposite. A concrete, text-supported contextual difference exists: A studied perimenopausal women without reported diabetes, while B studied patients with type-2 DM and found the adiponectin-lipid relationship modified by metabolic syndrome status, a population/metabolic-status difference that could plausibly explain the opposite sign.

source_evidence.quote: This study of 168 perimenopausal women utilized a cross-sectional design with non-random sampling.
Adiponectin negatively correlated with HbA1C, fasting blood glucose, insulin, and triglycerides.
A single center cross-sectional study was conducted on 173 patients with type-2 DM (82 males and 91 females).

Adiponectin was negatively correlated with waist circumference (r = -0.16, P = 0.06) and positively with HbA1c (r = 0.19, P = 0.032), total cholesterol (r = 0.23, P = 0.017), LDL (r = 0.30, P = 0.001), SD-LDL (r = 0.41, P < 0.001), and SD-LDL/LDL (r = 0.22, P = 0.023).
Significant interaction was observed between adiponectin and metabolic syndrome in relation to serum lipid profile.

verdict.label: apparent_contradiction
verdict.rationale: Both claims concern the association between circulating adiponectin and HbA1c, and both extractions accurately reflect their sources. The directions are opposite: study A (168 perimenopausal women, cross-sectional) reports adiponectin negatively correlated with HbA1C ('Adiponectin negatively correlated with HbA1C, fasting blood glucose, insulin, and triglycerides.'), while study B (173 patients with type-2 DM, cross-sectional) reports a positive correlation ('positively with HbA1c (r = 0.19, P = 0.032)'). Neither author states an explicit no-effect conclusion, so not_replicated does not apply. A concrete, source-supported contextual difference could explain the opposite signs: A examined perimenopausal women (generally without stated diabetes), whereas B examined patients with type-2 DM and additionally found that metabolic syndrome status significantly modified the adiponectin-lipid relationship ('Significant interaction was observed between adiponectin and metabolic syndrome in relation to serum lipid profile.'), making the differing metabolic/diabetic population a plausible explanatory difference rather than a pure contradiction.
